# Prior sensitivity (table-as-verdict)

<!-- allow-banned: meta-use (file: quotes forbidden phrases verbatim in the closing discipline note) -->

<!-- audit #43: --prior-sensitivity is now implemented; this file is regenerated from the same sweep the command runs (see TAST/scripts/regen_docs.py and model/bayesian_core.py:run_prior_sensitivity) -->
```bash
python -m model.bayesian_core --prior-sensitivity
```

## Stipulated-constant sensitivity sweep

Each declared stipulated constant (see `data/stipulated_constants.yaml`) is perturbed across its declared plausible range, holding all others fixed, and the maximum absolute change in the H1-H5 mechanism posterior is reported. The sweep runs over r in {0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5}; the table is ordered by descending influence.

| constant | sweep range | max |Δposterior| | influence | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `collapse_flat_target` | [0.3, 0.8] | 0.0532 | **HIGH INFLUENCE** | not inert at intermediate r (audit #31) |
| `beta_kappa_default` | [3.0, 30.0] | 0.0000 | low | mechanism-silent (floor term; does not move H1-H5) |
| `burial_site_confidence_floor` | [0.75, 0.95] | 0.0000 | low | mechanism-silent (floor term; does not move H1-H5) |
| `confidence_weight_source_class` | [0.25, 0.55] | 0.0000 | low | mechanism-silent (floor term; does not move H1-H5) |
| `confidence_weight_re_verifiability` | [0.2, 0.5] | 0.0000 | low | mechanism-silent (floor term; does not move H1-H5) |
| `confidence_weight_sampled_fraction` | [0.15, 0.4] | 0.0000 | low | mechanism-silent (floor term; does not move H1-H5) |

**Reading this table.** `collapse_flat_target` is the one constant that moves the mechanism posterior at intermediate r (audit #31) — it is marked HIGH INFLUENCE and carries `derivation_status: pending_derivation` in the manifest. The floor constants (erasure, genealogical n_eff, floor-shape terms) are mechanism-silent by construction: the physical floor does not rank H1-H5, so perturbing them moves the posterior by ~0. Declaring them is still required so the floor's assumptions are marked rather than buried.

## Prior-component sensitivity sweep (audit #42)

The H1-H5 prior (`RAW_PRIORS`) was, until v5.15, a code comment outside the manifest — *"not fitted to data; at r->0 posterior returns here."* It is now declared in `stipulated_constants.yaml`, fail-closed loaded, and swept. The table below perturbs each prior component across its declared range (renormalizing the five to sum to 1) at `sensitivity_reference_r`, and reports the max posterior delta. The prior components are all `pending_derivation` — the priors-work follow-on re-elicits each from cited evidence.

| prior component | sweep range | max |Δposterior| | influence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_prior_H5` | [0.250, 0.550] | 0.1234 | **HIGH INFLUENCE** |
| `raw_prior_H3` | [0.100, 0.300] | 0.0895 | **HIGH INFLUENCE** |
| `raw_prior_H2` | [0.050, 0.250] | 0.0387 | low |
| `raw_prior_H4` | [0.100, 0.300] | 0.0329 | low |
| `raw_prior_H1` | [0.030, 0.150] | 0.0059 | low |

_Measured at sensitivity_reference_r = 0.3._

_30 cells with delta >= 0.01 of 65 total; measured at r = 0.3._

**Reading this table — the named frontier.** The cells that actually move the posterior are the load-bearing surface of the model. They are the places where priors work must concentrate: every high-influence cell (delta > 0.05) is required to carry `derivation_status: pending_derivation` and is the named subject of the priors-work follow-on. The conclusion is robust only insofar as it holds across these cells' declared admissible ranges; a conclusion that flips inside a cell's range is fragile, and the cell that flips it is named here rather than buried in the CSV.

If posterior H1 stays ~0 until prior H1 exceeds ~0.9999, the engine is not balancing evidence against a prior — the likelihood product has already decided. Rebuild cells (Stream 1 first); do not add streams or tune priors.
